prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a chemically explicit change of pharmacological principle: event-driven removal of a protein by a designed molecule instead of occupancy-based inhibition. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept in 2001, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explained why molecular glues work and gave the field a second, independently confirmed mechanistic pillar. Heterobifunctional and glue degraders are now in many clinical trials, the VHL and cereblon mechanisms have been confirmed repeatedly in independent laboratories, and the concept has reached targets once considered undruggable. Colleagues with very different backgrounds (Aili, Linke, Somfai, Sparr, Zou, Chabes) all place it in their top four, so it has the broadest cross-subfield support, even though it won only two first places.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug has yet been approved, so the clinical proof is still pending and a prize could be read as early. Eight credited names and a three-person cap force hard omissions: Ciulli, Gray and Ito made decisive advances, and a trio that mixes the PROTAC strand (Crews, Deshaies) with the glue strand (Handa) can look like two discoveries squeezed into one citation. If the committee believes the PROTAC and glue strands cannot be reconciled, a mature and cleanly attributable topic such as B065 would be the safer choice.

responses.point: Opened with B065 (Pd-catalysed C-N coupling) as clear, mature and industrially pervasive, credit fitting Buchwald and Hartwig, with the Kosugi precursor questioned but not decisive.
responses.response: I agree B065 is the most cleanly attributable candidate on the list and I keep it as an alternative. My reservation is novelty of principle rather than quality: after the 2010 cross-coupling prize it is an exceptionally important extension of a recognised concept, whereas degradation establishes a new pharmacological logic. The Kosugi priority question is also not trivial. If degradation attribution cannot be settled, I would move to B065 without much resistance.

responses.point: Ranked B026 first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, noting that Handa, Ito and others made decisive cereblon contributions and the three-name cap forces a hard omission.
responses.response: We agree on the science and differ only on the third name. I chose Handa over Ciulli because identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target is the discovery that created the glue strand and explains a drug class used for decades, while Ciulli's VHL ligands, though excellent, refined an approach already launched by Crews and Deshaies. I accept that this leaves out Ciulli, who is arguably the strongest PROTAC mechanist, and I would not oppose his name if the committee prefers a pure PROTAC citation.

responses.point: Placed massively parallel sequencing (B037) first because Solexa chemistry (reversible terminators, clonal surface amplification) is chemistry-driven and its impact is exceptional.
responses.response: I agree that the impact of B037 is hard to exceed. My serious reservation is attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman are clear, but Mayer, Rothberg and Ju represent parallel routes, and the 1980 sequencing prize as a precedent leads some to see it as technology more than chemical discovery. A prize here risks arguments about who was left out that I find harder than the degrader allocation, so I keep it below B026.

responses.point: Put ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B045) first for turning lipid self-assembly physics into the delivery technology behind mRNA and siRNA medicines, crediting the Vancouver group.
responses.response: I rank B045 high, and I share your view that the lipid physical chemistry is real chemistry. The weakness is attribution, spread across Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer plus industrial work, and the 2023 Medicine prize already covered the vaccine headline. I would hold B045 as a second-part candidate or alternative, not as the lead.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a trio spanning the PROTAC strand and the molecular-glue strand, or insist on a narrower citation.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes recognition premature.
Whether B065 is judged novel enough given the 2010 cross-coupling prize, since it has the strongest opening support.
Whether Ciulli or Handa is the better third name.
statement.conflict_note: Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, but she ranks B056 first and none of my preferred or alternative candidates involves her work, so no specific conflict requiring recusal is apparent. I am Secretary and share the longest service with Johan Aqvist, which is not a candidate-specific connection.
